The failing test `testMySqlNullOutput` in `CSVPrinterTest` from Apache Commons CSV is testing the behavior when printing records with the value `null` using a specific format for MySQL. The test creates an `Object` array with the values `"NULL"` and `null`, sets up a CSV format for MySQL, creates a `CSVPrinter`, prints the record, and then checks the output against an expected string.

The current bug report mentions that the `nullString` in the CSV format should not be escaped, but the `CsvPrinter.printAndEscape` method incorrectly converts the null value to `"\\N"`. This results in unexpected behavior.

By looking at the code snippet of the `CSVPrinter.printRecord(Iterable<?> values)` method, we can see that it iterates over the values and prints each value without escaping. This indicates that the issue is likely related to how the `null` value is handled during the printing process when using the `CSVPrinter`.

To diagnose the issue further and pinpoint the root cause, we should investigate how the `CSVPrinter` handles `null` values during printing, especially in the context of the MySQL format configuration.

The potential fix for this issue would involve modifying the logic in the `CSVPrinter` class to ensure that the `nullString` is not escaped when printing records. 

The methods that would be the best locations to be fixed are:
```
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.CSVPrinter(java.lang.Appendable, org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat)
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.printRecord(java.lang.Iterable<?>)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
